title: CORE-Bench: Fostering the Credibility of Published Research Through a Computational Reproducibility Agent Benchmark

live_model.evidence: Sec. 4: 'We ran both AutoGPT and CORE-Agent using GPT-4o-2024-05-13 and GPT-4o-mini-2024-07-18 as LLM backends'; Table 5: 'CORE-Agent GPT-4o 60.00% 57.78% 21.48%'

prompt.location: Task prompts and level-specific hints described in Sec. 3-4; agent system prompts live in the released repository

claim.metric: pass@1 accuracy on the CORE-Bench-Easy test split (mean of 3 runs)
claim.location: Table 5, row CORE-Agent / GPT-4o, column CORE-Bench-Easy

notes: Each task runs an agent inside a VM with a $4 API cap (successful tasks averaged $0.54); re-execution needs the harness and Docker capsules, not just a prompt. n inferred from 60.00% and 57.78% being multiples of 1/45.

resolution.plan: The CORE-Agent prompts are printed in Appendix D.2, but the number depends on the released harness (per-task VM/Docker capsules, task questions, report grader) and the CORE-Agent code from the repository. Run the 45 CORE-Bench-Easy test tasks three times with gpt-4o-2024-05-13 under the $4 per-task cap and compare pass@1 with Table 5 (60.00%).
resolution.approximation: Agent trajectories are nondeterministic; capsule environments may have drifted; cost beyond the tier estimate.
